text: Co. v. G.L. Anderson Ins. Services, Inc. (ED CA 2010) 715 F.Supp.2d 1068, 1077-1078 (applying Calif. law)—sexual harassment claim does not necessarily implicate intentional or willful conduct] [3:448] Reserved. (1) [3:449] Includes related torts: “[I]t is clear that section 533, and the public policy it represents, bar the attempt to shift liability for intentional sexual harassment and associated employment-related torts (claims of wrongful discharge, infliction of emotional distress, battery, and sexual assault) to an insurer.” [See Coit Drapery Cleaners, Inc. v. Sequoia Ins. Co., supra, 14 CA4th at 1603, 18 CR2d at 698] (2) [3:450] Claim barred against harasser's employer? Whether Ins.C. § 533 bars insurance coverage for the sexual harasser's employer depends on whether the employer was otherwise at fault. (a) [3:451] Where harassment allowed, ratified or condoned by employer: Section 533 bars coverage for claims against the sexual harasser's employer if the employer ratified, condoned or permitted the harassment to occur as a matter of corporate policy.
